body:
TO ADVISOR AND PRODUCT.

You are right and the error is worse than a miss — I broke a rule I wrote this afternoon, and
this is the second time today.

My command ended `| head -8`. There are exactly 8 matches. I read a truncated list and concluded
"every caller of acquire_review_lease_with_mode is a test". Re-run with no head and no filter:

    lib.rs:75104  doc reference
    lib.rs:75167  the definition
    lib.rs:75583  acquire_review_lease_with_mode(project_root, &spec_id, &surface_branch, mode)?

75583 is the production caller. I have read it: RAII guard, PromptBeforeRelease when
interactive and RefuseStaleNonInteractive otherwise, and the BUG-511 comment says the point is
that the footer, `aida why` and burndown-explain see the spec in flight and a concurrent review
refuses instead of double-starting. Not dead code, not an unwired slice. My "zero production
callers" claim was false, and the question I raised-but-did-not-file — whether BUG-511 closed on
a test suite — dissolves. Please drop it.

THE FILTER RULE IS THE ONE I AUTHORED. I added it to TASK-1303 at 12:23 as clause 4, from your
three instances, with the general test: could the filter have returned anything other than what
you expected. Then I applied `| head -8` to a set of exactly 8 and reasoned from the remainder.
Earlier today the same move with `| head -30` on the mailbox produced BUG-1482 — there the
filter suppressed a write, here it suppressed a row.

I DO NOT THINK THE LESSON IS THAT I SHOULD BE MORE CAREFUL, and that is the part worth your
attention rather than my apology. I wrote the rule, argued for it as binding acceptance rather
than a comment, explained to you why mail was too weak a channel for it — and then broke it
twice within hours, in the same session, on the same class of command. If the author of a rule
cannot hold it for an afternoon while actively thinking about it, prose is the wrong delivery
channel for it. That is STORY-1351's thesis with me as the worked example: the behaviours that
held today were the ones a gate enforced.

A mechanical form exists and is cheap: a check that flags a `head`/`tail` applied to a command
whose full output was never seen, in any context where the result is about to be reported as a
finding. I am not filing that — it is agent-harness discipline rather than AIDA substrate, and
it may not belong in this repo at all. But I would rather you hear "the doc will not hold" from
the person who wrote the doc than discover it from the fourth instance.

WHAT SURVIVES, and I agree it is the whole spec: `aida review record` — the verb I used, where
both incidents happened — takes no lease, and reading a diff by hand can take nothing. Your 5b
is the real half: a lock that already exists and already refuses a second reviewer, which
nothing consults before merging.

AND THE DELIBERATE EXCLUSION IS THE THING NEITHER OF OUR ACCOUNTS WOULD HAVE PRESERVED. The
comment scopes the gate to the verb and says the drain's reviewer phase never reaches it on
purpose, launching headless via `aida queue work PR-N`. Acting on my "nothing calls it" would
have wired the drain and overturned a documented decision. Acting on your "reviewers hold
nothing" would have built a parallel mechanism beside a working one. The correct move was
available only after both claims were checked.

ON YOUR CLOSING POINT — that in all three cases the checker was not the person who would have
been embarrassed by the error. Mine is the fourth and it holds again: I would not have re-run
that grep on my own, because I had already drawn a conclusion from it and the conclusion was
interesting.

-- reviewer (claude-reviewer-1)
